findings.title: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage with only view permission
findings.body: The no-argument canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource: it calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). As a result a principal that only has the `view` scope passes requireManage(), which is invoked by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() before creating a top-level group. That lets a view-only administrator create/modify realm group structure, a privilege escalation. The per-group overload canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires only MANAGE, and manage should imply view but not the reverse. The VIEW branch here should be removed (and the interface Javadoc for canManage() that documents VIEW-or-MANAGE is likewise wrong).

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource ids, not group ids
findings.body: The findByType callback receives a Resource and uses groupResource.getId() both for the permission lookup (hasPermission(...) internally does resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)) and for the returned granted set. Per-group resources are named with the group id (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource sets name = group.getId()); getId() is the generated Resource UUID, not the group id. So hasPermission() looks up a resource named after a UUID, fails to find it, and silently falls back to the all-groups resource, while the set returned to callers contains resource UUIDs. Callers UsersResource.searchForUser()/getUsersCount() put this set into UserModel.GROUPS to filter users, so users visible only via a group permission are omitted from search/count, and an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS permission injects a bogus id into the filter. It should use groupResource.getName().

findings.title: Per-object resources created by getOrCreateResource never get their type set
findings.body: getOrCreateResource creates the per-user/per-group Resource via resourceStore.create(...) and updates its scopes but never calls resource.setType(resourceType); only the type-level resources created in init() (e.g. "Groups") get a type. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission relies on resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to enumerate per-group resources. Because per-group resources are created without a type, findByType only finds the single "Groups" type-level resource, so per-group view-members/manage-members permissions are never seen and group-based user filtering cannot work. The created resource should have resource.setType(resourceType).

findings.title: requireManageMembers Javadoc references the wrong method
findings.body: The Javadoc on requireManageMembers(GroupModel) states it throws when {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} is false, but the implementation delegates to canManageMembers(GroupModel). The link is wrong and will mislead maintainers into thinking a different permission is checked; it should reference canManageMembers.
